issues.text: Stronger flavours are worth trying: sauces, herbs, a squeeze of lemon. The evidence is mixed. One Dutch care home study found weight gain with flavour-enhanced meals; a later trial found no change.
issues.problem: Juxtaposition implies the mixed trial evidence tested sauces, herbs and lemon; the trials used commercial flavour enhancers, and the kitchen tips are untested (C13-23-f qualification).
issues.source_says: Mathey 2001 / Essed 2006: commercial flavour enhancers (and MSG) sprinkled on cooked meals in Dutch nursing homes; tips such as lemon and herbs not tested.
issues.replacement: Stronger flavours are reasonable to try (sauces, herbs, a squeeze of lemon), though these have not been tested. Two Dutch care home trials of commercial flavour enhancers gave mixed results: one found weight gain, a later one found no change.

issues.text: Stronger flavours such as sauces, herbs and lemon are worth trying; trial results are mixed.
issues.problem: Same conflation: trial results relate to commercial flavour enhancers, not sauces, herbs or lemon.
issues.source_says: C13-23-f: trials used commercial flavour enhancers; tips untested.
issues.replacement: Stronger flavours such as sauces, herbs and lemon are reasonable to try, though untested; trials of commercial flavour enhancers in care homes gave mixed results.

issues.text: In one small study of 32 people dying with cancer, mouth care, ice chips and sips relieved thirst in every case.
issues.problem: Drops 'usually': the source says symptoms were alleviated in all patients, usually by these means; the record's qualification says 'usually' belongs to the method. Also omits the 1994 date and no-comparison design.
issues.source_says: McCann 1994: 'In all patients, symptoms of hunger, thirst, and dry mouth could be alleviated, usually with small amounts of food, fluids, and/or by the application of ice chips and lubrication to the lips.'
issues.replacement: In one small 1994 study of 32 people dying with cancer, thirst and dry mouth were relieved in every case, usually with mouth care, ice chips and sips.

issues.text: In people aged 85 and over, sleeping in dentures was linked with more serious pneumonia. A link, not proof.
issues.problem: 'More serious pneumonia' reads as more severe pneumonia; the outcome was first hospital admission for, or death from, pneumonia. Also omits that these were people living at home in Japan.
issues.source_says: Iinuma 2015: 524 community-living people 85+ in Japan followed to first hospitalisation for or death from pneumonia; HR 2.38 (1.25 to 4.56), 48 events.
issues.replacement: In a Japanese study of people aged 85 and over living at home, sleeping in dentures was linked with more pneumonia needing hospital admission or causing death. A link, not proof.

issues.text: In a Japanese study of people aged 85+, sleeping in dentures was linked with more serious pneumonia. A link, not proof.
issues.problem: Same ambiguity: outcome was pneumonia leading to hospital admission or death, not more severe pneumonia.
issues.source_says: Iinuma 2015: first hospitalisation for or death from pneumonia.
issues.replacement: In a Japanese study of people aged 85+, sleeping in dentures was linked with more pneumonia needing hospital or causing death. A link, not proof.

issues.text: Note: in people aged 85 and over, sleeping in dentures was linked with more serious pneumonia; a link, not proof.
issues.source_says: Iinuma 2015 outcome: first hospitalisation for or death from pneumonia.
issues.replacement: Note: in a Japanese study of people aged 85 and over, sleeping in dentures was linked with more pneumonia needing hospital admission or causing death; a link, not proof.

issues.text: low-certainty evidence, and a few small studies pointed the other way.
issues.problem: Omits that the contrary studies were of other (mixed) tube types and very low certainty; reads as if some PEG studies showed longer survival.
issues.source_says: Davies 2021: three of four studies of mixed or unspecified tube feeding (310 participants) found longer survival; very low certainty.
issues.replacement: low-certainty evidence, and a few small studies of other tube types pointed the other way.

issues.text: Feeding tubes in severe dementia have not been shown to help people live longer or feel more comfortable, and one large study found slightly more pressure sores.
issues.problem: Drops the certainty qualifier and the observational nature; stronger than other versions.
issues.source_says: Davies 2021: no RCTs; survival evidence low certainty; pressure ulcers moderate certainty, one study.
issues.replacement: Feeding tubes in severe dementia have not been shown to help people live longer (low-certainty, observational evidence) or feel more comfortable, and one large study found slightly more pressure sores.

issues.text: If unavailable, 1.86 x (Na + K) + 1.15 x glucose + urea + 14 at 295 or more caught about 85 in 100 dehydrated people but flagged many who were not.
issues.problem: Missing units (mmol/L inputs; mOsm/L output) and that other common formulas performed poorly; record requires specifying this formula and units.
issues.source_says: Hooper 2015 BMJ Open: best of 39 equations in 595 older people; all in mmol/L; 295 mOsm/L sensitivity 85%, specificity 59%.
issues.replacement: If unavailable, estimate it: 1.86 x (Na + K) + 1.15 x glucose + urea + 14 (all mmol/L). At 295 mOsm/L or more it caught about 85 in 100 dehydrated people but flagged many who were not.

issues.text: In 188 UK care home residents, 1 in 5 were dehydrated on a blood test, and thirst did not predict it.
issues.problem: Source reports thirst was 'not associated'; 'did not predict' is a slightly different (diagnostic) claim.
issues.source_says: DRIE: 'Thirst was not associated with hydration status.'
issues.replacement: In 188 UK care home residents, 1 in 5 were dehydrated on a blood test, and thirst was not linked with it.

issues.text: Refusals did not stop, and mouth health showed no clear difference over three weeks. Research staff gave the care.
issues.problem: Omits that the main (primary) outcome of resistance also showed only a small reduction; the positive findings were secondary outcomes.
issues.source_says: Jablonski 2018: primary outcomes CRBs and oral health showed small effects (d=0.16, 0.18); assent, completion and duration were secondary.
issues.replacement: Refusals did not stop, and over three weeks neither resistance nor mouth health showed a clear difference. Research staff gave the care.

issues.text: In dementia, a review calls it promising but not yet shown in trials.
issues.problem: The review says studies were small and short with no definitive evidence; 'not yet shown in trials' slightly misstates (trials exist but are small).
issues.source_says: Bunn 2016: 'Promising interventions included ... family style meals'; 'no definitive evidence ... studies were small and short term.'
issues.replacement: In dementia, a review calls it promising, but the studies are small and short, so it is not proven.

issues.text: In dementia it is promising but not yet shown in trials.
issues.source_says: Bunn 2016: studies small and short; no definitive evidence.
issues.replacement: In dementia it looks promising, but the studies are small and short, so it is not proven.

issues.text: The largest trial tested a staff mouth care programme in 14 US nursing homes with 2,152 residents.
issues.problem: Omits that homes were chosen for high pneumonia rehospitalisation rates (record qualification).
issues.source_says: Zimmerman 2020: 14 North Carolina NHs 'that evidenced proportionately high rehospitalization rates for pneumonia'.
issues.replacement: The largest trial tested a staff mouth care programme in 14 US nursing homes with 2,152 residents, chosen for high rates of hospital readmission for pneumonia.

issues.text: A 2008 US trial found the same pattern: 42 minutes of mostly one-to-one help per meal, against about 5 minutes in usual care.
issues.problem: Does not say help was given by research staff for the 2008 figure (X mentions research team only for 2001).
issues.source_says: Simmons 2008: 'Research staff provided feeding assistance'; 42 minutes per person per meal.
issues.replacement: A 2008 US trial found the same pattern: research staff took 42 minutes of mostly one-to-one help per meal, against about 5 minutes in usual care.
